courses.summary: Learn how solar PV systems turn sunlight into electricity, what solar panels are made of, and how net metering works.

lessons.title: Photovoltaic systems
lessons.why: Solar installation, design and maintenance are growing green jobs as rooftop solar spreads to homes and businesses.
lessons.try: List the main parts of a rooftop PV system: panels, inverter, mounting and cabling.

lessons.title: Solar panels
lessons.why: Knowing how panels work — and what reduces their output, such as shade and dirt — helps you install and maintain systems well.
lessons.try: Look at a rooftop or solar farm near you and note which way the panels face and whether anything shades them.

lessons.title: Net metering
lessons.why: Net metering rules decide how much a household saves from solar, so installers and advisers need to explain them clearly.
lessons.try: Find your electricity provider's rules for exporting solar power and summarise them in two sentences.

quiz.q: In a PV system, what does the solar inverter do?
options: Converts direct current (DC) to alternating current (AC)
quiz.explain: The inverter converts the panels' DC output into AC.

quiz.q: Why do many utility-scale PV systems use tracking systems?
options: To follow the sun's path across the sky and generate more electricity
quiz.explain: Tracking the sun produces more electricity than fixed mounting.

quiz.q: Solar panels are made of modules of…
quiz.explain: PV cells produce excited electrons when exposed to light.

quiz.q: Which drawback of solar panels does the lesson mention?
options: They depend on the availability and intensity of sunlight
quiz.explain: Panels depend on sunlight, need cleaning and have high initial costs.

quiz.q: Net metering lets consumers who generate their own electricity…
options: use that electricity at any time, not only when it is generated
quiz.explain: Credits let daytime solar power be used later, for example at night.

courses.summary: Cut energy use and bills: efficiency basics, energy audits and how HVAC systems affect consumption.

lessons.title: Using energy efficiently
lessons.why: Using less energy for the same result saves money and cuts emissions — one of the quickest climate wins for any building or factory.
lessons.try: Walk around your home or office and list three ways energy is wasted (lights left on, open doors, old equipment).

lessons.title: Energy audits
lessons.why: An energy audit is the first step to finding savings, which makes auditors valuable to building owners and factories.
lessons.try: Read one month's electricity bill and note the total use in kWh and the cost.

lessons.title: Heating, ventilation and air conditioning
lessons.why: In hot, humid climates like Malaysia's, air conditioning is a large part of a building's electricity use, so efficient HVAC choices matter.
lessons.try: Check the thermostat setting where you work and find out what temperature it is set to.

quiz.q: Energy efficiency means…
options: using more energy for better results
reducing the amount of energy required to provide products and services
quiz.explain: Efficiency delivers the same products and services with less energy.

quiz.q: Which example of energy efficiency does the lesson give?
options: Insulating a building so it needs less heating and cooling energy
quiz.explain: Insulation keeps comfort while using less heating and cooling.

quiz.q: What are the two main motivations for energy efficiency named in the lesson?
options: Cost savings and lower greenhouse gas emissions
quiz.explain: Efficiency saves operating costs and supports climate action.

quiz.q: In commercial and industrial buildings, an energy audit is…
options: the first step in finding ways to reduce energy costs and carbon footprint
quiz.explain: Audits analyse energy flows to find savings opportunities.

quiz.q: HVAC stands for…
quiz.explain: HVAC systems regulate temperature, humidity and indoor air quality.

courses.summary: Understand ESG, how companies report on sustainability, and the widely used GRI Standards.

lessons.title: ESG explained
lessons.why: Investors, banks and large customers increasingly ask about ESG, so companies need people who can collect and report this information.
lessons.try: Pick a company you know and list one environmental, one social and one governance issue that matters for it.

lessons.title: Sustainability reporting
lessons.why: Sustainability reports turn activities into comparable information that builds trust with customers and investors.
lessons.try: Find the sustainability report of a listed company and note three things it measures.

lessons.title: The GRI Standards
lessons.why: GRI is among the most widely used reporting standards, so knowing its structure helps you prepare credible reports.
lessons.try: Visit the GRI website and find the names of the three groups of GRI Standards.

quiz.q: What do the letters ESG stand for?
quiz.explain: ESG covers environmental, social and governance issues.

quiz.q: In which 2004 report did the term ESG first come to prominence?
quiz.explain: "Who Cares Wins" was a joint initiative of financial institutions at the invitation of the UN.

quiz.q: Which criticism of ESG does the lesson mention?
options: Greenwashing and a lack of standardisation
quiz.explain: Critics point to data quality, lack of standardisation and greenwashing.

quiz.q: Sustainability reporting is the disclosure of…
quiz.explain: It reports environmental, social, economic and governance information.

quiz.q: The GRI Standards are organised into…
quiz.explain: GRI has Universal, Sector and Topic Standards.

courses.summary: Measure greenhouse gas emissions: carbon accounting, carbon footprints and GHG inventories.

lessons.title: Carbon accounting
lessons.why: You cannot cut what you do not measure. Carbon accounting is becoming a standard business skill as reporting requirements grow.
lessons.try: List the main sources of emissions in your workplace: electricity, fuel, travel and waste.

lessons.title: Carbon footprints
lessons.why: Footprints let you compare the climate impact of products, trips or companies in one common unit.
lessons.try: Use a free online calculator to estimate the carbon footprint of your daily commute.

lessons.title: Greenhouse gas inventories
lessons.why: An inventory is the organised list of emission sources that reports, targets and audits are built on.
lessons.try: Draw a simple table for an office inventory with columns for source, amount used, unit and emission factor.

quiz.q: Carbon accounting is…
options: a framework of methods to measure and track greenhouse gas emissions
quiz.explain: It measures and tracks how much greenhouse gas an organisation emits.

quiz.q: What do organisations often set before creating emission-reduction targets?
quiz.explain: They set a baseline, create targets and track progress.

quiz.q: Carbon footprints are usually reported in…
quiz.explain: Footprints use tonnes of CO2-equivalent per unit of comparison.

quiz.q: A product's carbon footprint covers…
options: only the day it is sold
its entire life cycle, from production to disposal
quiz.explain: It runs from production along the supply chain to consumption and disposal.

quiz.q: Greenhouse gas inventories combine different gases into one value using…
quiz.explain: GWP values weight each gas into a single emissions figure.

courses.summary: Understand electric vehicles, the lithium-ion batteries that power them, and how charging works.

lessons.title: Electric vehicles
lessons.why: EVs are spreading in public transport, delivery fleets and private cars, creating work in servicing, charging and batteries.
lessons.try: List the electric vehicles you have seen locally — buses, cars, motorbikes — and where they charge.

lessons.title: Lithium-ion batteries
lessons.why: The battery is the most valuable and safety-critical part of an EV, so battery knowledge is central to EV work.
lessons.try: Check the battery specification of a phone or laptop you own: its capacity and voltage.

lessons.title: Charging stations
lessons.why: Charging networks need planning, installation and maintenance — growing work for electricians and technicians.
lessons.try: Find the nearest public charging station on a map app and note whether it offers AC or DC charging.

quiz.q: What held back mass adoption of electric vehicles in the 20th century?
quiz.explain: Limited range hindered EVs, so combustion engines dominated for about 100 years.

quiz.q: Compared with other rechargeable batteries, lithium-ion batteries generally have…
options: higher energy density and a longer cycle life
quiz.explain: Li-ion batteries offer higher specific energy, energy density and cycle life.

quiz.q: The 2019 Nobel Prize in Chemistry recognised contributors to…
quiz.explain: The prize honoured the development of Li-ion batteries.

quiz.q: What are the two main types of EV charging stations?
quiz.explain: Stations supply either alternating current or direct current.

quiz.q: At an AC charging station, which part converts AC to DC to charge the battery?
quiz.explain: The onboard charger (OBC) converts AC from the grid into DC.

courses.summary: Use data and technology to farm smarter: precision agriculture, drip irrigation and drones.

lessons.title: Precision agriculture
lessons.why: Precision farming helps growers raise yields while using less water, fertiliser and fuel — important for food security and farm incomes.
lessons.try: Pick a crop grown near you and list two pieces of data that would help a farmer manage it better.

lessons.title: Drip irrigation
lessons.why: Delivering water straight to the roots saves water and nutrients, which matters more as droughts and costs rise.
lessons.try: Sketch a drip line for a small garden bed: water source, pipe, and an emitter beside each plant.

lessons.title: Agricultural drones
lessons.why: Drones can monitor crop health and spray precisely, cutting labour and chemical use.
lessons.try: List three things you would want a drone to photograph on a farm, and why.

quiz.q: Precision agriculture is a management strategy that…
options: uses only traditional methods without data
gathers and analyses plant, animal and field data to support farm decisions
quiz.explain: It combines temporal, spatial and individual data to improve decisions.

quiz.q: In farm fleet management, vehicles are equipped with…
options: a GPS tracking unit and an onboard controller that sends telemetry data
quiz.explain: Telematics send location, speed, engine hours and fuel use to a server.

quiz.q: Drip irrigation saves water by…
options: letting water drip slowly to the roots of plants
spraying water high into the air
quiz.explain: It places water directly in the root zone and minimises evaporation.

quiz.q: In which country was modern drip irrigation invented?
quiz.explain: The system used today was invented in Israel.

quiz.q: Agricultural drones use multispectral sensors to…
options: image radiation beyond the visible spectrum, such as near-infrared
quiz.explain: Multispectral sensors see beyond visible light to assess crop health.

courses.summary: Work with maps and location data: GIS basics, remote sensing and the free QGIS software.

lessons.title: Geographic information systems
lessons.why: Planning, utilities, agriculture, logistics and insurance all rely on location data, so GIS skills transfer across many sectors.
lessons.try: Think of a decision at work that depends on location (delivery routes, a new branch site) and the map data it needs.

lessons.title: Remote sensing
lessons.why: Satellites and drones provide up-to-date images for monitoring crops, floods, forests and cities.
lessons.try: Open a free satellite map of your area and look for changes compared with an older image.

lessons.title: QGIS
lessons.why: QGIS is free and open-source, so anyone can start learning professional GIS without a licence fee.
lessons.try: Install QGIS and open a free basemap of your town.

quiz.q: A GIS stores, manages, analyses and visualises…
quiz.explain: A GIS works with geographic data.

quiz.q: Which sectors use GIS according to the lesson?
options: Engineering, planning, transport and insurance, among others
quiz.explain: GIS supports many fields, from engineering to the natural sciences.

quiz.q: Remote sensing means acquiring information about an object…
options: without making physical contact with it
quiz.explain: It contrasts with on-site observation.

quiz.q: Passive remote sensing detects…
options: signals emitted by the sensor itself
quiz.explain: Active sensing emits its own signal; passive sensing detects reflected sunlight.

quiz.q: QGIS is…
quiz.explain: QGIS is free, open-source GIS software for Linux, macOS and Windows.

courses.summary: Move from 'take, make, waste' to circular thinking: principles, the waste hierarchy and recycling.

lessons.title: The circular economy
lessons.why: Circular practices cut costs and waste and open new business models such as repair, leasing and refurbishing.
lessons.try: Choose one product you use and list how it could be shared, repaired or reused before it is recycled.

lessons.title: The waste hierarchy
lessons.why: The waste hierarchy tells you which actions to try first: preventing and reducing waste beats recycling and disposal.
lessons.try: Rank three ways your workplace could handle paper waste, from most to least preferred.

lessons.title: Recycling
lessons.why: Good sorting and recycling recover valuable materials and lower emissions, but only when materials are clean and well separated.
lessons.try: Check which materials your local recycling service accepts and how they should be sorted.

quiz.q: A circular economy aims to…
options: extend product life by sharing, reusing, repairing and recycling
quiz.explain: It keeps products and materials in use for as long as possible.

quiz.q: Which is one of the three main principles of a circular economy?
quiz.explain: The principles: design out waste, keep materials in use, regenerate natural systems.

quiz.q: The waste hierarchy is usually presented as a…
quiz.explain: It is usually shown as a pyramid, ordered by preference.

quiz.q: Recycling is the process of…
options: converting waste materials into new materials and objects
quiz.explain: Recycling turns waste into new materials and objects.

quiz.q: In the 'Reduce, Reuse, Recycle' hierarchy, recycling is the…
quiz.explain: Recycling is the third step, after reducing and reusing.

courses.summary: Learn electrical fundamentals: current, Ohm's law and the safety devices that protect people.

lessons.title: Electric current
lessons.why: Electrical fundamentals are the base for solar, EV, IoT and building-services careers.
lessons.try: Find the current rating (in amps) printed on a phone charger or an appliance label.

lessons.title: Ohm's law
lessons.why: Ohm's law (V = IR) is used every day to size cables, choose components and find faults.
lessons.try: Calculate the current through a 12-ohm resistor connected to a 12-volt battery.

lessons.title: Residual-current devices
lessons.why: RCDs save lives by cutting the power when current leaks, so knowing how they work is basic electrical safety.
lessons.try: Find the RCD in your home or office distribution board — look for a test button marked 'T'. Do not open the board.

quiz.q: Electric current is…
options: a flow of charged particles through a conductor or space
quiz.explain: Current is the flow of charged particles such as electrons or ions.

quiz.q: In SI units, electric current is measured in…
quiz.explain: The ampere (amp) is the SI unit of current.

quiz.q: Ohm's law is written as…
quiz.explain: Voltage equals current times resistance.

quiz.q: A 12-volt battery is connected to a 12-ohm resistor. What current flows?
quiz.explain: I = V / R = 12 / 12 = 1 ampere.

quiz.q: A residual-current device (RCD) interrupts a circuit when…
options: the current in the line and neutral conductors is not equal
quiz.explain: An imbalance means current is leaking to ground or through a person.
